user.title: Solis MK5 Local
user.description:
Home Assistant asks the stick for fresh data every 10 seconds. For that it needs the stick's IP address and serial number. Choose one of two ways:

**With push (recommended).** Keep the port below. In the stick's web interface, point a free Remote Server slot (e.g. Server C) at your Home Assistant IP address (Settings > System > Network) with this port, connection type TCP. Leave IP address and serial number empty: they are learned from the stick's first push (within ~6 minutes), and followed when the stick gets a new IP address.

**Without push.** Leave the stick's Remote Server settings alone, and fill in its IP address and serial number below. The serial number is the number in the stick's own Wi-Fi network name, AP_<serial>. Give the stick a fixed IP address in your router.

error.port_in_use: This port is already in use, choose another one.
error.host_and_serial: Fill in both the IP address and the serial number of the stick, or leave both empty.
error.cannot_connect: The stick did not answer on TCP port 8899. Check the IP address and the serial number, and that Home Assistant can reach the stick. Right after one of its own pushes the stick is silent for about 20 seconds; if everything looks right, just try again.

abort.already_configured: A listener on this port is already configured.

init.title: Solis MK5 Local options
init.description: Polling asks the stick for fresh data every few seconds (TCP port 8899). It finds the stick by itself from its pushes: now {learned_host}, serial {learned_serial}. Only fill in host and serial for a stick that does not push to Home Assistant; a filled-in host is no longer followed when the stick changes address. The staleness window decides when live measurements go unavailable without any data; energy totals always keep their value.

data.scan_interval_seconds: Poll every this many seconds (0 = off, minimum 5)
data.stale_after_minutes: Mark measurements unavailable after this many minutes without data
data.host: Stick IP address (empty = learn from pushes)
data.logger_serial: Stick serial number, as in its Wi-Fi name AP_<serial> (empty = learn from pushes)

incompatible_logger.title: Solis logger sends an unrecognised protocol
incompatible_logger.description: Several frames in a row from your Ginlong/Solis stick failed validation. This usually means the connected logger uses a different firmware or hardware revision than this integration was built for, so its data cannot be parsed reliably. Enable debug logging to see the rejected frames as hex dumps in the Home Assistant log.
